# Golden outputs from Rust 0.3.4

These files record the behaviour of the Rust core before it is deleted in G6. Every file is generated by
`crates/finglass-core/src/golden/mod.rs`; nothing here is written by hand.

The top-level `*.json` files are the older G0a/G0c goldens. They stay where they are and are generated by
`crates/finglass-core/src/db/go_fixtures.rs`, not by this generator. Everything in a sub-folder belongs to a
migration area.

## Regenerating

```text
cargo test -p finglass-core write_goldens -- --ignored
```

`cargo test -p finglass-core goldens_are_current` regenerates every file twice in temporary directories, checks that
the two runs are identical, and diffs the result against this folder. It fails when a Rust change leaves a stale
golden behind.

## Inputs

`testdata/inputs/<area>/` holds the inputs the generator reads. The statement files are copied from the Rust tests
(`crates/finglass-core/tests/import_*.rs` and the `#[cfg(test)]` modules) or are synthetic statements created for
this milestone. No real account data is used. Where a Rust test builds a value inline, the file keeps the test's
name or a short description of it.

## Files

All files are pretty-printed JSON with two-space indentation and a trailing newline.

### `import/statements.json`

`import::read(file_name, bytes, None, 2026-10-15)` for every file in `testdata/inputs/import/`. Each entry has the
detected format, format label/detail, account IBAN(s), skipped rows, pending count, the CSV layout (delimiter,
charset, headers, column mapping), the CAMT closing balance and every booking with all its fields. Among the inputs
are one file per supported CSV bank preset (Sparkasse, ING, DKB, HVB card, comdirect, Commerzbank, N26, FinDesk's
own export), content detection without a file extension, MT940, CAMT.052, CAMT.053, a CAMT ZIP, OFX SGML/XML, QIF
and XLSX.

### `hash/hashes.json`

`transaction_hash`, `import_hash` and `hashes(iban, bookings)` from `import/hash.rs` for every booking of every
import golden, keyed by file and index, plus the byte-exact edge cases: empty partner/purpose, umlauts, NFC vs NFD,
trailing spaces, a negative zero, `0.10` vs `0.1`, newlines and tabs.

### `dedup/reports.json`

The import service's duplicate decisions (`import::import` and `import::dedup`) on the overlapping statements from
`tests/import_statement_import.rs`: first import, re-import, an overlapping file, and a re-import after a deleted
booking. Each step has every count, the updated balance and the summary text; the final stored rows are listed too.

### `format/formats.json`

`format::money`, `whole_money`, `percent`, `shares`, `date`, `date_time` and `iban` over a value grid in EN, DE and
FR; `parse_date`, `parse_decimal` and `parse_amount` over valid and invalid strings; `money::parse_decimal` and
`money::format_plain` per currency.

### `iban/ibans.json`

`iban::normalize`, `is_valid`, `format` and `mask` over `testdata/inputs/iban/ibans.txt` (47 strings: valid IBANs
from the tests, check-digit-valid synthetic IBANs with obviously fake bank codes, invalid checksums, spaces,
lower case, foreign countries, too short, not an IBAN).

### `rules/files.json`

`RuleFile::parse` and `RuleFile::write` for every rule file in `testdata/inputs/rules/` (round trip, BOM + CRLF,
comments and blank lines, every row-error kind, the import workflow file and the default rule set). The re-export is
the exact text `RuleFile::write` produces.

### `rules/matcher.json`

`RuleMatcher` decisions on the 110 bookings in `testdata/inputs/rules/bookings.csv` over the 12 rules of
`default_rules.tsv` (index, selected rule/pattern, category), plus the PayPal/shop cases from
`rules/matcher.rs`.

### `rules/payment_providers.json`

`PaymentProviders::shop_match`, `title_of` and `merchant_of` for the marker, pre-comma, card, top-up and
non-PayPal cases in `rules/payment_providers.rs`.

### `bank_text/bookings.json`

`bank_text::display_partner`, `display_purpose`, `display_description` and `secondary_line` on every booking of
every import golden, keyed by file and index.

### `balance/charts.json`

`balance::RunningBalance::compute`, `balance::BalanceHistory::from_running` and `BalanceHistory::compute` on the
three multi-month statements (`balance_checking_2026.csv`, `balance_savings_2026.csv`, `balance_card_2026.csv`),
including the bank differences.

### `recurring/detections.json`

`RecurringDetector::detect` and `upcoming(..., 30)` on the monthly, quarterly and irregular histories in
`testdata/inputs/recurring/`, with `today` fixed to 2026-10-15.

### `receipt/receipts.json`

`receipt::parse(text, EUR, 2026-11-07)` on the 22 receipt texts in `testdata/inputs/receipt/` (German, French and
English, from the tests plus synthetic receipts): total, date and every distinct amount.

### `dashboard/months.json`

`dashboard::load_dashboard` for October 2026, September 2026, July 2026 (a month without bookings) and January 2026
(the carry-forward month), over a throwaway encrypted database that imported three account statements, the 24
default categories, the default rules and two budgets. Every figure is recorded, including recent transactions,
the category splits, the six-month bars, budgets, recurring payments and the carry-forward.

### `report/reports.json`

`report::build_report`, `build_tax_report`, `build_tax_bookings` and `monthly_report` for 2025 and 2026 (and
December 2025 / October 2026 for the monthly report), plus `sum_by_category` and `category_shares` in EN and DE.

### `export/exports.json`

The exact CSV text for 2026 in EN and DE (`report::csv::export_range_to_csv`, including the UTF-8 BOM); the cell
values of both sheets of the tax-bookings XLSX (`TaxReportExporter::export_xlsx`, read back through the XLSX
reader); and the extracted text and page count of the tax-bookings PDF and the report PDF (`extract_text` and
`inspect`), not the PDF bytes.

### `i18n/keys.json`

Every `i18n::Key` variant, sorted by name, as `{key: {en, de, fr}}`, using `i18n::text` for each language.

### `bank_directory/lookups.json`

`bank_directory::parse` on `testdata/inputs/bank_directory/blz-test.txt` (fixed-width ISO-8859-1 records with an
umlaut, an extra-branch record, a deleted record and a short line) and `fints_blz` lookups, including the
HypoVereinsbank branch that maps to the central BLZ.

## Randomness

Nothing in these goldens is random. The throwaway dashboard database lives in a temporary directory whose path is
never recorded, and no timestamps, UUIDs or salts are written.
